touches.text: gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.

ROOT INTENTION for checks and gates (Akien, 2026-10-27): the inspector does all the checks, so there is no need for more checks anywhere else. The inspector's output is consumed by the gate. The gate's output is the certificate. "This was how I meant it all along."
The certificate is one file type you can't write. It carries a cryptographic (or similar) way to say that the right code wrote it, on this date, at this time, with these hashed findings.
That signing belongs in the base gate class, so every gate has it.
Entry gates exist only to kick back what doesn't meet the entry requirements. Nothing in them is about who writes what.
[Q#61: The crossing (today transitions.emit: move the cursor, journal it) is neither the inspector's nor the gate's. Is it the ticket's own act, recorded on the strength of the certificate?]
base proxy: the base class for every proxy device, a device that is the one way to a service (13).
build_inspector: python sieves run after a build; reds a component that fails one (no charter, no proofs, a silent device, ...). "We find a new thing, we add a new sieve." → CodeMother (10.3.5)

Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, diagnostic_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve. [Q#31: all of these to CodeMother? See 17.]

"it owns the gates only because we had to have some place to put them, but it does not control anything." The gates refuse on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10: "the gate is the refuser but it's doing so on behalf of the ticket. so the ticket owns the refusal.")
VERBS: crossing, watch, clear. clear is the PROVED gate it houses on the ticket's behalf.
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10). The gates are housed in harbor_master.
